teaching.hint: Which tree positions are farthest from the leaves at both ends of a longest path?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The minimizing roots are the one or two centers of a tree; removing all current leaves together preserves those centers.
solution_outline.approach: Build degrees and adjacency, then repeatedly remove a whole layer of degree-one vertices until at most two vertices remain. Return the survivors; handle the single-vertex tree directly.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The queue holds exactly the leaves of the current reduced tree; each round deletes one complete outer layer and preserves its center set.
solution_outline.correctness: Every longest path loses one endpoint at each end per round, so its middle vertices remain. A tree has one or two such centers, exactly the final survivors.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time and `O(n)` space; each vertex enters one layer and each edge is considered at most twice.
solution_outline.pitfall: Removing newly exposed leaves in the same round can shift the center.

common_wrong_turns: Root a traversal at every vertex
source_fidelity_notes: The statement’s output order is unrestricted and `n=1` is retained explicitly.
